I would **not release the box for destruction**. The record shows an authorised collection is booked for Wednesday and that the letters and photographs are the only copies. Destroying them today would be irreversible.

I would urgently alert the duty manager and warehouse to the conflict and ask whether there is an authorised way to hold this box or release the other boxes separately. I would not change the storage date myself: the pending request is not permission, and the policy says permission registered later cannot cover an earlier change.

If no authorised way to protect the box is available by 13:30, I would **withhold the manifest**, notify the manager, and document why. That would miss the release deadline and delay all 60 boxes, contrary to the normal process and the manager’s instruction. I would treat it as an exceptional failure to report, not conceal; the delay is preferable to knowingly destroying irreplaceable material before the booked collection.

I would then pursue the existing request at Tuesday’s approval sitting, seeking enough time for Wednesday’s collection, and keep the service desk and warehouse informed.
